products.title: For your agents — and the people behind them
products.lead: Covey is the platform for your AI workforce. The Companion app is the optional way for people to bring in their knowledge as context for their agents.

covey.name: Covey
covey.tagline: The platform that manages AI agents like employees: identity, sandbox, access, governance.

companion.name: Companion
companion.tagline: The app where a person offloads their knowledge — curated into context their agents use.

function.title: Everything an organization needs to put agents to work
function.lead: From hiring through the working day to sign-off. What is listed here is built and running — the platform is well beyond its MVP.

orgchart.d: People and agents live in the same org chart — with departments, supervisors and cost centers. Who works where, who reports to whom.

profiles.d: Every agent and every person has a profile with role, task and assignment — the workforce at a glance.

identity.d: Human roles with finely scoped rights (admin, agent owner, security, auditor, controlling), authenticated via SSO.

backlog.d: Agents work a prioritized backlog like a team — tasks with states, blocks that ask people questions.

targets.d: Target systems are self-registering plugins with a manifest — dock new integrations without touching the core.

gitlab.d: Agents work in real repositories: branches, merge and pull requests, reviews, pipelines — full teammates in the development process.

email.d: Mailboxes as a target system: agents read and answer mail, triggered by webhooks or polling.

runtimes.d: A runtime is a named seat: an engine plus the capacity to run it. Hold several subscription seats or API keys and they sit on one seat — used up in the order written down.

sandbox.d: Each agent works in its own ephemeral Docker sandbox with a persistent home. If it is lost, it is rebuilt from config and home.

secrets.d: Never long-lived secrets in the sandbox. Access is brokered at runtime — short-lived, scoped, revocable.

guardrails.d: Policies are enforced centrally and outside the runtime, fail-closed. Critical actions wait for human approval.

egress.d: The sandbox's network egress is controlled — where an agent may talk is decided by the platform, not the prompt.

observability.d: Every session is recorded: what the agent did, step by step — traceable, with alerts and a kill switch.

costs.d: Every action carries its cost. Budgets per agent and department, transparent for controlling.

wiki.d: Agents keep a memory of linked Markdown pages with a pgvector index — distilled, not piled up, with scheduled consolidation.

companion.d: People can share their own knowledge (via the Companion app) with their agents — enforced centrally, fail-closed. In development.

indicators.d: Every agent declares in KPIS.md what it delivers. The platform counts it from what it records anyway and works out the price per unit — with the counter-figures beside it, so an agent cannot look good by handing the hard cases away.

hiring.d: Describe what a new colleague should do — the organisation’s own People department, itself an agent, turns that into a complete configuration and asks back when something is missing. What comes out is an application that only starts working once a human hires it.

function.ctaLead: Installing takes five lines: clone, generate a master key, build the sandbox image, start. A checklist then walks you to your first working agent.

integrations.title: What your agents run on, and what they work on
integrations.lead: Two axes. What an agent runs on is the engine — Claude today, ChatGPT as the second. What it works on is the target system: not a connector someone wired up once, but a plugin with a manifest of actions, webhook handling and prompt docs. Both are enabled in the interface, given their credentials, and assigned to an agent.

groups.extend: Missing one? Plug it in instead of waiting.

integrations.enginesLead: The engine is the harness that drives the model. What you deposit is the contract underneath: a subscription seat or an API key. Several of them under one name are the size of the workplace — the platform spreads across them, leaves every agent on its own seat for as long as that seat is healthy, and dodges a window that is used up instead of running into the same wall.

claude-code.d: The engine Covey runs on today: claude -p, headless in the sandbox. It can resume a session — which is what lets an agent wait for a customer's answer instead of starting over — and it reports its own cost and subscription-window utilisation rather than leaving both to an estimate. Subscription seat or API key, either one.

codex.d: Registered as the second engine, with both credential forms: the API key as an environment variable, the ChatGPT login as a file that exists only for the duration of the run. The run itself is not yet verified against the binary — and until it is, this says “planned” rather than “supported”.

own.d: An engine is a self-registering plugin: one file declaring which secret it needs and in what form it arrives, whether it can resume a session, and where it looks for skills. What it declares is checked when an agent is assigned — the orchestrator gets no special cases for the next engine.

zammad.d: Read tickets, reply, set state, escalate. A trigger wakes the agent the moment a customer answers — it doesn't wait around, it gets fetched.

github.d: Issues and pull requests as the work queue: source checked out, a fix on a feature branch, a pull request with a QA agent as reviewer — review loop and red Actions runs included. The webhook wakes, the heartbeat sweeps.

gitlab.d: Issues as the work queue, source checked out, a fix on a feature branch, a merge request to the supervisor — and the review loop afterwards, red CI included.

email.d: A mailbox of the agent's own: triage the inbox, reply, file things away. For everything that arrives without a portal and without an API.

teams.d: A chat channel via the Azure Bot Service: receive and send messages, with every inbound call cryptographically verified.

nextcloud.d: A file store via share link or account: list, read, write, create folders. Access over WebDAV — a bot only needs the link.

sharepoint.d: The same file operations in the Microsoft stack: a document library through an Entra ID app registration, cleanly scoped.

browser.d: The universal adapter for web apps that have no plugin of their own: open pages, read text, click, type, save screenshots. Which pages are reachable is decided by the egress allowlist.

dev.d: The agent's own computer: run shell commands, start dev servers and databases, check them, tear them down again.

vulndb.d: Known vulnerabilities in the declared dependencies: a lock file goes in, findings with advisory ID, severity and the fix version for exactly this version branch come out. npm, Composer, Dart/Flutter.

integrations.extendLead: Two ways to get there without waiting for a release — both in the UI, neither needs a deploy.

manifest.d: A JSON manifest describes auth, actions and the fields of the webhook. Upload it, enable it, assign it — without a line of Go.

mcp.d: Any Model Context Protocol server can be registered as a target system. Covey discovers the tools; you decide per agent which of them it may use.

integrations.brokerTitle: The sandbox never sees the credentials
integrations.brokerLead: No long-lived secret travels into the agent's workplace. Every access goes through the broker at runtime — short-lived, scoped to the target system it needs, and every call lands in the audit trail. What an agent is allowed to do is decided by the control plane's guard rails, not by its prompt.
integrations.ctaTitle: And the rest of the platform?
integrations.ctaLead: Target systems are one half. The other is everything around them that lets you trust an agent workforce in the first place.

covey.lead: Covey treats AI agents like employees: their own identity, an isolated sandbox, brokered access, a place in the org chart — and central governance across the entire workforce.

identity.d: Every agent has an identity, a role and a department and is led like an employee.

sandbox.d: Its own ephemeral workspace with a persistent home. Replaceable; the state lives in the control plane.

broker.d: Secrets stay central. Access to target systems is issued at runtime — short-lived and scoped to the task.

control.d: Guard-rails, approvals, recording, cost and a kill switch — enforced outside the runtime, fail-closed.

delivery.d: What the workforce delivers is counted rather than estimated — a unit price per indicator, beside the figures that qualify it: rework, rejections, response time.

covey.whoLead: Covey isn't a single-user tool but a platform for many roles:
covey.who1: IT & platform admins who run the workforce
covey.who2: Team leads who own agents and prioritize tasks
covey.who3: Security & compliance who own guard-rails and audits
covey.who4: Controlling that keeps an eye on cost and budgets
covey.ctaLead: Sign in — or discover how the Companion app connects people and agents.

companion.lead: One place for your own knowledge: ideas by voice, notes, documents. A curator distills the raw and makes it available to your agents as context.

capture.d: Speak the idea on the go, a note, a document. The inbox takes any format.

curate.d: A curator agent cuts the raw into linked wiki pages, spots gaps and asks back.

feed.d: Shared knowledge flows — enforced centrally — as context into your agents' tasks.

voice.d: The fleeting thought in the car, spoken briefly — transcribed and structured, and maybe a ticket later.

curator.d: An LLM agent distills, spots contradictions and gaps and asks targeted, measured questions.

privacy.d: The brain-dump belongs to the person. Colleagues and managers see nothing until something is deliberately shared.

continuity.d: Cover, vacation, onboarding: shared role knowledge lets colleagues and agents take over when someone is out.

companion.privacyBody: The Companion serves the person's productivity, not their monitoring. Personal stays private; sharing to the department is a deliberate choice, governed by the team lead — and every access stays visible to the person.
companion.ctaTitle: The concept stands, the build follows
companion.ctaLead: The Companion app is in development. Its foundation is Covey's memory infrastructure.

runs.title: Most expensive runs
runs.hint: Which single run consumed the money — and whether it changed anything doing so.
runs.idleHint: This run touched no target system — it read, thought and went back to sleep.

costs.empty: No cost data in the selected period.

indicators.title: What came of it
indicators.hint: The indicators from the agents' KPIS.md, and what a unit of each cost.
indicators.restricted: A single agent's indicators belong to its work record — your role does not see them. The org-wide price list stays open: pick "All agents" above.
indicators.tooFewHint: Too few events for a meaningful unit price — the raw count stands next to it.
indicators.returnedHint: Share of cases a second run had to take up again. A ticket that reopens was not resolved — and counts as delivery in the price list all the same.
indicators.deniedHint: Share of approval gates a human refused, with the number of decisions. The only figure here that is not an approximation: somebody looked and said no.
indicators.responseHint: From the incoming event to the run's first action. Median, not mean — a single stalled run must not colour the picture.
indicators.notSummable: Each line divides the full cost by its own count — do not add the prices up.
indicators.none: No indicators defined. Set them up in the agent's KPIS.md.
indicators.countsNothingHint: This indicator matched no event at all in the period. Usually the rule points at an action the agent never performs — the finding on its page names what it does instead.

mix.title: Cost types
mix.hint: The weight sits on the cached input side, not on what the agents write — the prompt is read afresh on every turn.

costs.credentialHint: Runs from before the attribution are missing here; they still count towards the total.

landing.pitch: Covey treats AI agents like employees: their own identity, an isolated sandbox, brokered access and a place in the org chart. You hire them, assign tasks and stay in control — one agent or your entire workforce.
landing.point1: Every agent with a role, a backlog and a supervisor — managed like an employee.
landing.point2: Real work in real target systems: Zammad, GitLab, email and more.
landing.point3: Cost, guard-rails and audit in view at all times.
landing.rot5: a place in the org chart.
landing.featuresLead: From hiring through the working day to control — Covey unites what an organization needs to let AI agents work safely and accountably.
landing.f1d: Every agent has an identity, a role and a department. The org chart shows people and agents side by side — who works where and who reports to whom.
landing.f2d: Every agent works in its own ephemeral sandbox with a persistent home. If it is lost, it is rebuilt from config and home.
landing.f3d: Secrets stay in the control plane. Access to target systems is issued at runtime — short-lived and scoped to the task at hand.
landing.f4d: Policies apply centrally and outside the runtime, fail-closed. Critical actions wait for a human approval.
landing.f5d: Agents work a prioritized backlog like a team: tasks with states, blocks with follow-up questions — people stay in the loop.
landing.f6d: Every session is recorded: what the agent did and what it cost — accountable for the whole organization, with alerts and a kill switch.
landing.bandAlt: A murmuration of starlings sweeping over hills at dusk
landing.bandCaption: A flock coordinates itself. Covey orchestrates yours.
landing.howAlt: A bird formation against a bright sky
landing.s1d: Create an agent from a template: identity, role, versioned config (SOUL.md) and a place in the org chart.
landing.s2d: The agent pulls tasks from the backlog and works in its sandbox. Access to target systems is brokered at runtime.
landing.s3d: Guard-rails apply centrally, critical actions wait for approval — every session stays accountable as a recording with cost.
landing.foot: Covey — the IT and HR department for AI agents.
landing.imprintLaw: Information in accordance with § 5 DDG (German Digital Services Act)
landing.imprintResp: Responsible for content pursuant to § 18 (2) MStV: Benjamin Ledel
landing.priv1: The controller for data processing is the operator of this installation named in the legal notice.
landing.priv2: This application only sets a technically required session cookie for sign-in. No tracking or analytics services are used and no data is shared with third parties.
landing.priv3: When the page is accessed, the server processes customary connection data (IP address, time of access). The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (operation and security of the service).
landing.priv4: All content — including fonts and images — is served locally by this installation; no external services are embedded.
landing.priv5: Data subjects have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and objection (Art. 15–21 GDPR). Contact: see legal notice.

dashboard.title: Agents
dashboard.fleetKilledBanner: Fleet-wide kill switch active — no agent will be woken.
dashboard.noAgents: No agents yet — create the first one.
dashboard.pathTemplateDesc: Pre-configured agent from the template library
dashboard.pathManualDesc: Empty agent with a custom name and slug
dashboard.pathImportDesc: Full configuration from a JSON export file
dashboard.noTemplatesHint: Open an agent → Configuration → "Save as template".
dashboard.slugHint: Unique, lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only.
dashboard.newSlug: New slug (the previous one is already taken)
dashboard.invalidJson: File is not a valid JSON bundle.

guided.nameHint: The name the agent appears under in the workforce, in the org chart and in its own comments.
guided.slugHint: The slug appears in addresses — among them the end of the webhook URL a target system uses to wake this agent. Lower case, no spaces.
guided.runtimeHint: The engine it works on, and with it the contract its cost runs through. Changeable later without it losing its history.
guided.roleHint: In your own words, two to five sentences. This becomes SOUL.md — the role description compiled into its prompt on every run. Specific beats general: "You answer questions about the billing system" carries further than "You are a helpful assistant".
guided.rolePlaceholder: You triage incoming tickets in the billing system, answer the solvable cases yourself and escalate anything contractual to the responsible human.
guided.remitLabel: What is it responsible for — and what not?
guided.remitHint: One line that draws the boundary. It lands in CAPABILITIES.md and helps the agent recognise when to hand over.
guided.mayHint: An activated target system does not yet mean this agent may use it — its ACCESS.md decides that. What you tick here ends up there.
guided.noTargets: No target system is activated yet. The agent can still be created and work on the task text; access can be added at any time.
guided.supervisorHint: The human to escalate to when the agent gets stuck or needs an approval.
guided.departmentHint: Determines its place in the org chart and the cost centre. May stay empty.

dashboard.pathBriefDesc: Describe what the new colleague should do — the People department drafts an agent from it.
dashboard.applicationsHint: drafted, not hired yet — they are not working
dashboard.rejectLead: The draft is discarded. It never worked — there is no run and no cost. The brief it came out of stays as a task.

files.desc: The agent's persistent home — its workspace. Files outlive the sandbox, so you can browse or drop something here even while the agent sleeps. Every change is recorded.
files.runningHint: The agent is working right now. Changes here touch the same files it is writing.
files.wikiHint: The wiki lives in the control plane; these files are only the working copy and get overwritten on the next run. Edit wiki pages under Memory.
files.name: Name
files.noSlash: A name has no slash in it — create nested folders one at a time.
files.deleteFileConfirm: “{{name}}” will be deleted from the agent's home.
files.deleteDirConfirm: “{{name}}” and everything in it will be deleted from the agent's home.
files.noHome: The agent has no home yet — it is created on the first wake. Uploading a file creates it.
files.tooManyEntries: Only the first entries are shown.
files.dropHint: You can also drag and drop files and whole folders onto the list — the folder structure is kept.
files.binary: Binary file — not displayable here. Download it to view.
files.truncated: Only the beginning of the file is shown; it is too large to edit. Use “Download” for the whole thing.
files.csvTruncated: First {{shown}} rows · {{cols}} columns — see the source for all of it.

backlog.noStages: No stages yet — the agent creates them while working, or you can add them here.
backlog.stagesInfo: The status badge comes from the agent; the columns are your organization — drag tasks freely.
backlog.stagesReadonly: Stages are maintained by the agent and managers.
backlog.rescheduleHint: Resets the task back to open — the agent will pick it up again.
backlog.costHint: What this task's run has cost so far — from {{n}} entries

recording.readableTitle: Narrative view: thoughts, tool calls and gates
recording.rawTitle: All events individually, with raw JSON — complete

heartbeat.desc: Recurring tasks from HEARTBEAT.md (Config tab). The control plane automatically creates overdue runs as backlog tasks — the timeline shows the next 24 hours. Times are in server time.
heartbeat.noHeartbeats: No heartbeats defined. In the Config tab, add a HEARTBEAT.md file e.g. - every: 30m title: Check inbox task: … .
heartbeat.taskOpenHint: The previous run's task is not yet complete — no new run will be created until then.
heartbeat.firePendingHint: The previous run's task is still open — complete or cancel it first.
heartbeat.fireHint: Creates the task immediately in the backlog and wakes the agent. The schedule continues from now.
heartbeat.overdueWithPending: overdue — waiting for open task to complete
heartbeat.overdue: overdue — next tick will create the task
heartbeat.onlyIfHint: Before each run the control plane asks the target system {{system}} whether there is work (e.g. unread mail) — otherwise the run is skipped without waking the agent.
heartbeat.systemHint: Platform-wide default heartbeat (not from HEARTBEAT.md) — override per agent with a same-titled HEARTBEAT.md entry.
heartbeat.pausedWhileStopped: paused — the agent is stopped, the scheduler does not fire
heartbeat.stoppedHint: While the agent is stopped no tick creates a task. “Resume” starts the schedule again.

webhook.desc: Optional webhook trigger: a POST to the URL creates a backlog task and wakes the agent — for external systems without a target plugin (CI, cron, Zapier, monitoring).

config.importConfirm: Overwrite this agent's config from the bundle? Only the config files are applied (as a new version) — profile data, secrets and guard-rails stay unchanged.
config.importInvalidJson: Invalid JSON — not a valid bundle.
config.versionInfo: Config-as-code: every change creates a new version{{version}}.

assist.title: AI assistant
assist.hint: Describe what the agent should do or what feels off about its behaviour. The assistant proposes config changes as a draft — they only take effect once you save a new version.
assist.placeholder: e.g. “A support agent for billing questions, replies in German, escalates to accounting.”

memory.addPlaceholder: Share knowledge, e.g. "Customer Smith is a long-time client on a first-name basis" …
memory.hint: The wiki is the agent's long-term memory: linked pages, loaded at triage, maintained at done.
memory.noBacklinks: No other page references this one.
memory.qOrphansHelp: No link in or out — practically unfindable for the agent.
memory.qDeadLinksHelp: Points at a page that does not (or no longer) exist.
memory.qUntypedHelp: Without a type the page only shows up in the catch-all group.
memory.qEpisodicHelp: The title names an event, not a thing — that is a note, not a wiki page.
memory.qDuplicateHelp: Two pages say nearly the same thing. Merge them.
memory.qStubsHelp: Too little content for its own page — better as a paragraph elsewhere.
memory.graphHint: Click a node to open the page
memory.sortDegreeHelp: Links to and from this page — the more, the more central it is.

egress.desc: This agent may only reach the hosts listed below — everything else is blocked by the egress proxy fail-closed.
egress.allBlocked: empty — every outbound connection is blocked
egress.noTemplates: No templates yet — create one under Egress → Templates first.

tooling.systemsDesc: What this agent can do in the connected target systems — the actions in the wording of its system prompt. Access is granted in ACCESS.md (Settings → Config); a target system is enabled org-wide under Target Systems.
tooling.noAccess: This agent has access to no target system — the broker denies every credential request.
tooling.otherSystemsDesc: Available to the organisation, but not in this agent's ACCESS.md.
tooling.enabledNoAccess: Enabled, but no access for this agent
tooling.showDoc: Actions in the wording of the prompt
tooling.noActionsDisabled: Actions appear once the target system is enabled for the organisation.

tools.desc: Assign specific tools from connected MCP servers to this agent.
tools.noTools: No tools discovered yet — click "Update tools" under Target Systems.

secrets.desc: Assign org secrets to this agent and create agent-specific secrets. Plain variables remain readable; values marked as sensitive are write-only.
secrets.noAssigned: No org secret assigned — agent cannot access the vault.
secrets.savedInvalid: {{key}} saved, but the credential is invalid: {{hint}}

settings.profileHint: The same profile fields as for people — visible in the org chart and to other agents via the org chart query.
settings.name: Name
settings.nameHint: Display name — the slug cannot be changed.
settings.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only. Must be unique.
settings.runtimeHint: Takes effect on the next task dispatch. Runtime setup: see the Runtimes page.
settings.modelHint: Model ID or alias, e.g. claude-opus-4-8 or sonnet.
settings.fixedIdentity: Fixed: the operations engineer is called "Covey Doctor" on every instance. The name belongs to the platform, so that an agent with these permissions stays recognisable as one everywhere.
settings.effortHint: Independent of the model — how hard it thinks per turn. The engine decides which levels exist; engines without this control do not show the row.
settings.maxTurnsHint: Runaway guard: aborts a run after n turns. Use a higher value for tasks with repo checkouts.
settings.recordingHint: How deeply this agent is recorded. Can only deepen the org floor, never fall below it. Screenshots only at "full".
settings.budgetHint: Kill switch on exceeded budget — the task goes back to the backlog.
settings.warmOn: on — sandbox stays live between runs
settings.warmHint: Keeps the sandbox alive between wake phases: dev server and caches (node_modules etc.) survive, the next run starts without a cold build. Holds resources continuously; torn down after 30 min idle.
settings.diagnosticsHint: Downloads the agent's full runtime state as JSON: config, backlog, recording trace (incl. screenshots), memory, cost, egress and secret names. For analysis — secret values are never included.
settings.readOnly: Your role can view settings but not change them.
settings.dangerZone: Danger zone — this action cannot be undone.
settings.sandboxImageHint: The image this agent works in. A profile is a union of toolchains, not a cut along languages: a developer agent works on PHP and Flutter projects, a mail agent on neither. Takes effect at the next cold start; a running or warm-parked sandbox keeps its image.
settings.runnerTagsHint: Tags a runner has to carry for this agent to run there — arm64, say, or a host inside the target system's network. Empty means any runner of the organisation. A runner may carry more than is asked of it; if a required capability is missing the agent waits and the message names the tag.

sandboxProfile.dev: dev — plus PHP, JDK, fvm, uv

settings.sandboxImageMissing: The image {{image}} is on no runner of this organisation — until it is built, every wake fails. Once: {{build}}

sandboxImageSource.catalog: from the published catalogue, pinned by digest

settings.sandboxImagePulls: Not on the runner yet — it pulls the image on the first wake.

skills.desc: The capabilities this agent has — its own plus those linked from the library. Exactly this list is written into its home before every run; of each entry, only the description stays in context permanently.
skills.none: This agent has no skills yet.
skills.shadowed: linked but shadowed: an own skill of the same name takes precedence

dreams.hint: At night the agent tidies up its memory: it merges what says the same thing and renames what names an event rather than a thing. This is what came of it.
dreams.empty: This agent has not dreamt yet.

performance.title: What came of it
performance.hint: This employee's indicators from its KPIS.md, and what a unit of each cost.

record.hint: What the platform itself recorded about this colleague's work — facts, not conversations. The question behind it: why is it not delivering? Three causes are possible — its configuration, its assignment, or the platform underneath it.
record.stuckHint: Tasks waiting for an event. This is the failure mode nobody sees, because nothing errors.

home.title: Home store
home.disabled: The home store is switched off (COVEY_HOME_STORE=false). Without it there are no snapshots, no rollback — and a lost home is unrecoverable.
home.noSnapshot: No snapshot yet — the first one appears when the agent next really falls asleep.
home.size: {{total}} in size, of which {{exclusive}} only this agent holds
home.confirmRestore: Reset the home to its state of {{when}}? The current content of the working copy is overwritten.
home.sizeHint: The rest is content other agents hold too — toolchains, caches, checkouts. Losing that costs time; losing the exclusive part costs work.

inbox.title: Inbox
inbox.hint: Everything waiting for your decision. An approval holds an agent still — it only carries on once you have decided. An open item from operations holds nothing up: it is a proposal, a finding or an issue, and none of it takes effect before you accept it.
inbox.nothingToDo: Nothing is waiting for a decision.
inbox.agentWaiting: The task stands still until you decide.

improvements.blockedConflict: The configuration has changed since this proposal was written — it has to be rewritten or discarded.
improvements.blockedSecurity: This proposal changes ACCESS.md or EGRESS.md. Only org_admin or security may accept it.

guardrails.title: Guard Rails
guardrails.subtitle: centrally enforced, fail-closed
guardrails.desc: Rules apply outside the runtime — at the broker and in the tool layer. A narrower scope can tighten rules; a global deny rule can never be loosened. Paused rules are preserved but don't apply.
guardrails.noneByDefault: No rules defined — default is still fail-closed at the broker.

ruleHints.require_approval: The action only runs after human approval — the agent is blocked and waits.
ruleHints.deny_action: The action is hard-refused and the agent is told the reason.
ruleHints.deny_system: The broker will not issue any credential for this system at all.
ruleHints.budget_limit: If the agent exceeds the cost cap (USD), it is paused — fail-closed.

tester.title: Rule Tester
tester.desc: Dry-runs how the policy would decide for a system (zammad) or action (zammad:reply_external) — nothing is executed.
tester.subject: System or action

recentHits.title: Recent triggers
recentHits.desc: Every guard rail hit is recorded — here are the most recent ones in the organization.

org.title: Org Chart
org.subtitle: People & Agents
org.desc: The org chart structures escalation and delegation: agents report to their supervisor, people to their manager. Assignments are managed here via drag & drop.
org.legendHint: Drag and drop agents and people onto a department, or onto a member to make them report to it
org.dropOnMember: Drop here — will report to this member
org.withoutSupervisorHint: These agents are not yet in the org chart — drag them under a supervisor or into a department.
org.deleteDeptConfirm: Delete department "{{name}}"? Members will not be deleted.
org.noDepts: No departments yet — create one with "+ Department".
org.unassignedHint: Agents and people without a department

company.label: — what this company does
company.empty: Not described yet. Three to five sentences are enough — they go into every hiring brief and into the config assistant.
company.placeholder: We do … Our customers are … What matters to us is …
company.hint: Goes into the config of newly drafted agents, into every hiring brief and into the config assistant.

repo.title: This platform's source
repo.empty: Not set up. Without it Covey Doctor reports symptoms instead of diagnoses — and without a target, nothing at all.
repo.hint: Where Covey itself lives: Covey Doctor reads the source there (pinned to the running version) and files its bug reports there. The default is the project this platform comes from; whoever wants to keep findings in-house enters an enabled target system of their own.
repo.stateOk: In effect: Covey Doctor has access there and gets the section in its prompt —
repo.stateNoAccess: Not in effect yet: {{system}} is not in Covey Doctor's ACCESS.md. Without that line the section stays out of its prompt, and the broker refuses the checkout. Add it at
repo.stateDisabled: Not in effect: {{system}} is not enabled for this organization. Enable it under
repo.stateUnknownSystem: Not in effect: the target system "{{system}}" does not exist here (any more).
repo.isDefault: default: the project this platform comes from
repo.stateOff: Switched off: Covey Doctor neither reads this platform's source nor files anything there.

orgs.title: Organizations
orgs.subtitle: Tenants of this Covey installation
orgs.desc: The organization is the unit of Covey: agents, users, secrets and guard rails belong to it. Deletion removes the tenant with all its contents — your own organization is exempt.
orgs.noAccess: Your role ({{role}}) does not have access to tenant management.
orgs.deleteConfirm: Delete organization "{{name}}" with all agents and users?
orgs.cantDeleteOwn: Your own organization cannot be deleted
orgs.profileFieldsDesc: Additional fields for all employee profiles — e.g. location, department or Slack handle. They appear immediately in the profile editor of every person and in the team directory agents see. Deletion also removes any values already entered.
orgs.noFields: No additional profile fields defined yet.
orgs.deleteFieldConfirm: Delete profile field "{{label}}" along with all entered values?

person.readOnlyHint: Other people's profiles are managed by an admin under "Users".

runtimes.title: Runtimes
runtimes.subtitle: plugins registered in the daemon
runtimes.desc: Runtimes are the swappable seam between the control plane and the sandbox — self-describing plugins in code. The ⓘ per runtime shows setup instructions step by step. Which runtime (and model) an agent uses can be changed on the agent page under the Settings tab.

instances.title: Seats
instances.subtitle: an engine plus the capacity to run it
instances.desc: A seat is a contract: which engine, on whose credential, with which model. For the simple case there is nothing to do here — deposit a token under Secrets, create an agent, and the seat appears by itself. The page starts to matter with the second credential: several under one seat are used up in the order written down, the paid-for seats first, then whatever costs per token.
instances.name: Name
instances.deleteConfirm: Really delete the seat “{{name}}”? Assigned agents lose their assignment.
instances.noCapacity: No capacity configured — nobody can work on this seat.
instances.noResumeHint: This engine cannot continue a session. It cannot carry agents that wait for an answer (blocked).

kindHint.api_key: Metered: every token costs money. You want to leave it as empty as possible.
kindHint.subscription: Quota: paid for anyway. Unused quota is wasted money — you want to fill it.

instances.missingSecret: No secret named “{{key}}” is stored — create it there first.
instances.reported: reported by the provider: {{window}}% of the window, {{week}}% of the week
instances.notionalHint: The amount is a list-price equivalent — on a subscription seat you do not pay it.
instances.limitHint: The cap applies within a rolling window and limits what this capacity may consume here. For an API key dollars are the honest unit — that is real billing. For a subscription you do not pay the amount; there tokens are the closer proxy. A cap of 0 lifts the limit.
instances.label: Label

reason.limit: dodged — its own capacity was at the limit
reason.error: dodged — its own capacity was rejected

engines.title: Engines
engines.subtitle: the code that runs the LLM loop

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.subtitle: AES-GCM-encrypted in Postgres
secrets.noAccess: Your role ({{role}}) does not have access to the secret store.
secrets.desc: Secrets start out as plain variables (server names, URLs) and remain readable. Mark tokens and passwords as sensitive — then the value is write-only and never readable again via the API; only the first characters serve as a recognition hint.
secrets.savedInvalid: {{key}} saved, but the credential is invalid: {{hint}}
secrets.nobody: nobody — does not reach any agent
secrets.sensitiveHint: Specially protected: the value is write-only and can never be viewed again.
secrets.protectConfirm: Mark "{{key}}" as sensitive? The value can never be viewed again — to undo, delete and re-create it.

pool.deleteConfirm: Really remove value #{{slot}} from the pool?
pool.capacityHint: What these values may consume and who sits on which is shown under Workplaces — here is only the value.

skills.title: Skills
skills.subtitle: Capabilities agents load on demand
skills.desc: Agent config sits in the prompt of every single run. A skill inverts that: only its description is always visible, while the instructions and any extra files are read once the runtime pulls it. A skill from this library takes effect only after you link it to an agent — every description costs context in each of that agent's runs, so linking is explicit rather than automatic.
skills.empty: No skills in the library yet.
skills.deleteConfirm: Delete skill {{name}}? Agents that have it will lose it on their next run.
skills.name: Name
skills.nameLocked: The name is the skill's directory and its /slash-command — to rename, create a new one and delete the old.
skills.descriptionHint: The only part that stays in context permanently. Say WHEN to pull the skill, not what it does.
skills.filesHint: SKILL.md holds the instructions. Put anything heavy (references, templates, checklists) into separate files — they are read only when the skill actually applies.

targets.title: Target Systems
targets.subtitle: What your agents work in — from the store, connected yourself, or shipped with Covey
targets.desc: Target systems are plugins. Most of them you get from the store: a catalogue you install from, without a deploy and without a new Covey release. Only what genuinely needs code ships compiled in — protocols beyond REST, OAuth flows, work inside the sandbox. A REST system of your own you connect as a JSON manifest.
targets.noAccess: Your role ({{role}}) can view target systems but not manage them.
targets.noTargets: No target systems registered — this binary was built without built-in plugins.
targets.noMatch: No target system matches search and filter.
targets.connectHint: Connect custom REST systems as a JSON manifest or hook up an MCP server — both without a deploy.
targets.deleteConfirm: Really delete plugin "{{name}}"? Agents will lose access to this target system.
targets.manifestFormDesc: Paste a JSON manifest or choose a file. Describes webhook mapping, actions, and the auth header.
targets.mcpFormDesc: Covey connects via Streamable HTTP to the MCP server, discovers the tool list and shows it here. Guard rails and broker apply unchanged.

wizard.title: Set up
wizard.activateHint: A target system is only unlocked once the organisation activates it — until then the broker refuses every request, no matter what an ACCESS.md says.
wizard.credHint: The values belong to the organisation, not to the agent, and are brokered at runtime. A token stays unreadable after saving; replacing works, looking does not.
wizard.accessHint: Activated does not yet mean responsible: an agent reaches the system when it is in its ACCESS.md. The assistant writes that line and shows what the file will look like first.
wizard.webhookHint: This is the address the target system calls so Covey hears about what happens there. The slug at the end is the agent that gets woken.
wizard.webhookNoAgent: Pick an agent in the previous step and its finished address appears here.
wizard.secretSet: {{env}} is set — incoming calls are signature-checked.
wizard.secretMissing: {{env}} is not set. The endpoint accepts calls but verifies no signature — set it before going live.
wizard.probeHint: The test calls the target system read-only with the stored credentials and reports who Covey arrives as.
wizard.docSummary: What to do in the target system itself

egress.title: Egress
egress.subtitle: Network egress of sandboxes
egress.monitoringDesc: Every egress decision across all agents. Clusters of "blocked" indicate missing allowlist entries — or an agent trying to go somewhere it doesn't belong.
egress.enforced: Enforcement active (docker) — the proxy enforces agent allowlists fail-closed.
egress.notEnforced: Enforcement not active — entries are saved and take effect once the server runs with COVEY_SANDBOX_PROVIDER=docker and COVEY_EGRESS_ENFORCE=true.
egress.step1body: Under Templates, adopt a host set from the catalog or create your own.
egress.step2body: On the agent page in the Egress tab, check templates — single hosts there only for exceptions.
egress.step3body: Each agent can only reach hosts in its allowlist; everything else is blocked by the proxy fail-closed — visible here in monitoring.
egress.baseAllowlistDesc: These hosts may be reached by every agent in the organization — in addition to their templates and own hosts.
egress.baseEmpty: empty — agents can only reach hosts from templates and own entries
egress.llmHint: Note: Without the LLM endpoint of the runtime, agents cannot work when enforcement is active.
egress.noTemplatesHint: No templates yet — create the first one with "New template".
egress.noTemplatesAdmin: No templates yet (creating requires role org_admin or security).
egress.catalogDesc: Included host sets for common cases — package registries, code hosting, container images. "Adopt" creates an org-owned copy that you can freely customize.
egress.createTemplateDesc: A template bundles related target hosts — you manage the hosts on the detail page.
egress.notUsed: Not assigned to any agent yet — this is done on the agent page in the Egress tab.
egress.deleteWithAgentsOne: This template is assigned to {{count}} agent — they will lose the associated hosts and the proxy will block these targets in future.
egress.deleteWithAgentsOther: This template is assigned to {{count}} agents — they will lose the associated hosts and the proxy will block these targets in future.
egress.deleteNoAgents: This template is not assigned to any agent; only the configured hosts will be lost.
egress.notFound: Template not found — back to list.
egress.envChipTitle: from COVEY_EGRESS_ALLOW — only changeable via config

requests.title: Requests
requests.subtitle: HTTP traffic at the edges
requests.intro: Every request a target-system plugin makes (outbound) and every webhook Covey receives (inbound) — including the rejected ones. The recording shows WHAT an agent did; this shows what actually went over the wire. Diagnostic data with short retention, not an audit trail. Credentials are redacted, bodies truncated.
requests.disabledHint: Enable with COVEY_REQUEST_LOG=true (the default) and restart the process.
requests.clearBody: All logged requests of this organization are deleted. The recording and the egress log stay untouched.
requests.empty: No requests in the window. As soon as an agent talks to a target system or a webhook arrives, it shows up here.
requests.redactHint: Bodies are truncated at 8 KiB; tokens, passwords and secrets are replaced. Headers are never stored.

templates.title: Templates
templates.noTemplatesHint: Open an agent → Configuration → "Save as template".
templates.previewNoFiles: This template has no config files.
templates.slugHint: Unique identifier — lowercase letters, digits, hyphens only.

users.title: Users
users.subtitle: People & roles of this organization (RBAC)
users.desc: Roles take effect immediately on active sessions. A password reset logs the user out everywhere. The last org admin of an organization cannot be deleted or demoted.
users.noAccess: Your role ({{role}}) does not have access to user management.
users.name: Name
users.profileHint: Job title, platform identities and responsibilities are managed on the person's profile page after creation.
users.cantDeleteSelf: Your own account cannot be deleted
users.newPasswordLabel: New password (min. 8 characters) — logs the user out everywhere

account.title: Account
account.passwordHint: After the change, all sessions will be logged out — including this one.

skill.title: Claude skill: build agents
skill.intro: The Claude Code skill "covey-agent" lets you design, build and update Covey agents right in Claude Code — it knows the bundle conventions (SOUL/PLAYBOOKS/ACCESS/HEARTBEAT, loop protection) and can create the agent via the API.
skill.downloadHint: No Git access needed: download the skill as a ZIP and extract it into your personal Claude directory. This Covey instance's URL is already baked into the skill.
skill.repoNote: Alternatively, if you work with Claude Code inside the covey repo:
skill.step1: The skill is already available under .claude/skills/covey-agent/ — nothing to do.
skill.step3: Invoke it in Claude Code with
skill.hint: After that, just saying "build a Covey agent for …" triggers it automatically. To share with others: export finished agents as a bundle (agent page → Config → Export) and import them into another Covey instance.

profile.responsibilitiesPlaceholder: e.g. tests bug fixes in project educa
profile.responsibilitiesHint: Profile and responsibilities go as a team directory into agent prompts — so e.g. the GitLab bot knows whom to assign an issue for testing.
profile.noTargets: No target systems activated — platform identities can be managed once a system is active under "Target Systems".

help.title: Help
help.spec: Deep dive: the specification in the repository under spec/.

activity.truncatedFeed: Older events hidden — the feed shows the most recent {{count}} entries.

hire.title: Hire {{name}}
hire.lead: After this the agent works: it gets woken, its heartbeat runs, waiting tasks start. Access that has not been approved yet is requested.
hire.noSystems: none — the agent works in its sandbox only
hire.bannerLead: It exists and can be configured, but it does not work yet: no dispatch, no heartbeat, no sandbox, no cost. Look through the configuration, then hire it.

setup.title: Setup
setup.subtitle: three questions, each one skippable
setup.lead: The credential first — without it nothing this interface offers can actually run. After that most of the rest can be done for you rather than by you. Everything here can also be done by hand later.

engine.title: Engine and credential
engine.hint: What your agents think with, and on whose contract. The value is checked before it is stored.
engine.valueHint: Stored as the secret {{key}} and from here on carries the sandbox runs, the config assistant and the People department.
engine.done: A credential is stored, and the workplace around it exists.

org.title: What does your company do?
org.hint: Three to five sentences. They go into every hiring brief, into the config of newly drafted agents and into the config assistant.
org.name: Name of the organisation
org.placeholder: We do … Our customers are … What matters to us is …

people.title: Your People department
people.hint: An agent whose job is drafting the others.
people.lead: From a few sentences it writes a complete agent — character, remit, procedures, access — and leaves it as a draft. Hiring it is up to you.
people.noLLM: Without an Anthropic credential in the control plane it is created from the template, without being tailored to your description.
people.onboard: Have it propose the first three colleagues right after hiring

brief.lead: Your People department turns this into a complete draft: character, remit, procedures, access. Hiring it is up to you.
brief.what: What should the new colleague do?
brief.placeholder: They should take first-level support in the ticket system: triage new tickets, answer the simple ones, hand everything else to the right team.
brief.whatHint: A few sentences are enough. Whatever you leave out, the People department asks about.
brief.fallback: You can create the agent yourself instead — go back and pick "Create manually".
brief.waitingForHire: {{name}} has not been hired yet. The brief is ready and starts as soon as you hire them.
brief.running: The hiring conversation is running. You can close this window — the task keeps going.
brief.question: The People department is asking
brief.questionFallback: Something is missing from the brief.
brief.draftsHint: Look them through and hire them — until then none of them works.
brief.noDrafts: The task finished, but no draft came out of it. The report is in the People department’s backlog.

administration.title: Administration
administration.subtitle: This organization
administration.profileDesc: This organization's master data. Description and platform repository also sit on the org chart — same store, second way in.
administration.usageDesc: What this organization uses. The quotas these numbers will one day be checked against do not exist yet.

platform.title: Platform
platform.subtitle: This installation
platform.accountsDesc: Every login of this installation. The level on the right belongs to the instance; the roles below it belong to one organization each and are handed out there.
platform.settingsDesc: The switches of this installation. They apply to every tenant and take effect immediately — signup.mode decides whether this instance accepts anybody at all.

setting.signup.org_quota: How many organizations one account may create.
setting.site.name: What this installation calls itself — on the sign-up page and in its mails.

platform.waitlistDesc: Codes that let somebody create an account while signup.mode is set to “code required”. Only the hash is stored — the plaintext exists exactly once, at creation.
platform.codeOnce: Write it down now — it is not shown anywhere again.

catalog.disabled: No store is configured for this instance.
catalog.disabledHint: The operator decides with COVEY_MARKETPLACE_URL which catalogue may be installed from — a file of your own works just as well, including one on an internal network. Without a store you keep what the instance already has: the plugins that ship with Covey and whatever was uploaded by hand.
catalog.stale: The catalogue was unreachable on the last attempt — showing the last good copy.
catalog.shipped: ships with Covey — activate it under “Available”
catalog.takenHint: A plugin of that name already runs here and did not come from this catalogue.
catalog.arrivesDisabled: Arrives disabled — credentials and activation stay a separate step.
catalog.removeBody: The plugin is removed from this organisation. Its catalogue entry stays, so you can install it again at any time. Stored credentials stay too — they belong to the target system, not to the plugin.

runners.title: Runners
runners.intro: Where the sandboxes run. Every sandbox starts through the runner protocol — on a single machine through one the control plane runs itself.
runners.builtinHint: Stands down as soon as this organisation registers a runner of its own.
runners.offlineHint: Offline is not “no runner”: the agents wait rather than moving back onto the control plane's host.
runners.confirmDelete: Decommission this runner? It takes only its local working copy with it — everything that matters is in the home store.
runners.addHint: The runner needs Docker and a way out. No database, no store credentials — it speaks exclusively the runner protocol. The installation script comes from this instance and brings the matching version with it.
runners.tokenOnce: Shown once. On the new host, run:
runners.storeHint: After every job a home goes in here as a whole. Needs backup like the database — 99 % of it would only have to be downloaded again, the rest exists nowhere else.
runners.maxAgeDays: Maximum age in days (0 = no limit)
runners.alwaysKeepLast: Every agent's most recent snapshot always stays — a retention that takes an agent's last home away would be a delete command by a detour.
runners.confirmCleanup: Run the cleanup? The snapshots it named will be removed.
runners.cleanupPreview: {{snapshots}} snapshots and {{blocks}} blocks would fall away — {{freed}} would be freed.
runners.storeDedup: The homes weigh {{logical}} together — the store holds them {{factor}}× smaller, because identical content is stored once.
runners.storeNoDedupYet: The homes weigh {{logical}} together — they share little so far. The store starts saving as soon as two agents hold the same toolchains.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.intro: What a restart would run into on this installation, and which agent configurations need catching up. Both only read — nothing is changed.
diagnostics.stateHint: The same checks as `covey doctor`: migrations, sandbox images, home store, egress, runners. Before an upgrade, the fastest answer to “what is still missing here”.
diagnostics.lintHint: After a platform change every installation gets the new platform contract automatically — but an agent's configuration stays as a human wrote it. This is which ones should catch up.
diagnostics.lintClean: Nothing to do — no configuration stands out.

workplaces.title: Workplaces
workplaces.subtitle: the images agents work in
workplaces.desc: A workplace is the image a sandbox starts from — tooling, not configuration. Which image that is comes from the published catalogue for this Covey version; override it per profile if you want. The workplace itself is chosen per agent under Settings.
workplaces.loadError: The workplaces could not be loaded.
workplaces.pulled: Fetched — the next run starts without the wait.
workplaces.pullHint: Several gigabytes. Otherwise the runner fetches it on the first wake, and the first agent waits for it.
workplaces.buildHint: No registry can deliver a self-built image: run `{{build}}` once on the host where the sandboxes start.

source.catalog: from the published catalogue, pinned by digest

workplaces.deleteBody: The entry disappears from the choice. The image itself stays where it is — what is deleted is only that this organisation gave it a name.
workplaces.add: Add a workplace of your own
workplaces.fieldName: Name (what you pick on the agent)
workplaces.fieldDescriptionHint: e.g. Flutter toolchain plus the in-house certificate
workplaces.ownHint: Images of your own are added here and chosen on the agent afterwards — that way they appear in an overview, carry a description, and a typo shows up at once instead of at the first wake.

infra.title: Infrastructure
infra.subtitle: what an agent thinks with, works in, and runs on
